canonical_statement: The study aimed to compare SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation with DPP-4 inhibitor initiation for all-cause mortality, all-cause hospitalisation, and 59 long-term conditions across 17 systems in adults with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aim of this target trial emulation study was to investigate the effects of SGLT-2i, against DPP-4i, on all-cause mortality, all-cause hospitalisation, and risk of 59 long-term conditions across 17 systems.

canonical_statement: The source population comprised adults aged 40 years or older with type 2 diabetes who received an SGLT-2 inhibitor or DPP-4 inhibitor between 12 November 2012 and 31 December 2023.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The source population comprised individuals aged 40 and above with a diagnosis of T2DM who received DPP-4i or SGLT-2i between 12th November 2012 and 31st December 2023.

population.label: Adults aged >=40 years with T2DM initiating SGLT-2i or DPP-4i in England, 2012-2023

canonical_statement: Individuals were excluded for same-day initiation of both drug classes, a recent prescription of the comparator within 180 days before index, index within 12 months of practice registration, type 1 diabetes, or end-stage kidney disease at baseline.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Individuals who have initiated two compared drugs on the same date or had a recent prescription of the comparator drug (within 180 days prior to the index date), whose index date is within 12 months after the registration date, or those who had type 1 diabetes or end-stage kidney disease at baseline were excluded.

population.label: Eligible new users of SGLT-2i or DPP-4i
exclusion_criteria: Same-day initiation of SGLT-2i and DPP-4i
Comparator prescription within 180 days before index
Index date within 12 months of registration

canonical_statement: The intervention strategy was new-user initiation of an SGLT-2 inhibitor, with index date defined as the first SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The index date of the treatment group was defined as the first prescription date of SGLT-2i.

exposures.details: New-user initiation; index date = first SGLT-2i prescription

canonical_statement: The active comparator strategy was new-user initiation of a DPP-4 inhibitor, with index date defined as the first DPP-4 inhibitor prescription.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the index date of the comparator group was defined as the first prescription date of DPP-4i.

exposures.details: New-user initiation; index date = first DPP-4i prescription

canonical_statement: The target trial emulation used CPRD Aurum primary-care electronic health records linked to HES Admitted Patient Care and ONS Death Registration data in England.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we used primary care electronic health records (EHRs) from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum linked with the Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care (HES-APC) dataset and Office of National Statistics (ONS) Death Registration Data

canonical_statement: Propensity-score fine-stratification weighting targeted the average treatment effect; logistic propensity scores were estimated from baseline covariates, non-overlap was trimmed, and 50 equally sized propensity-score strata were used for weighting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Create 50 equally sized propensity score stratums, after ranking the entire cohort based on the propensity score.

canonical_statement: Variables with no more than 20% missingness were multiply imputed by chained equations into five completed datasets under a missing-at-random assumption.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Multiple imputation using the chained equation method was used for missing data of all variables with less than or equal to 20% missing values, with 5 simulated complete datasets being created, under the assumption of missing at random.

canonical_statement: The main analysis used a per-protocol strategy with each prescription providing 180 days of treatment coverage; follow-up ended at the earliest outcome, transfer/data exit, death, study end, discontinuation, or comparator initiation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We defined treatment status by using a per-protocol approach, in which we considered each prescription to provide 180 days of treatment coverage.

canonical_statement: Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, first hospitalisation, and the overall number of hospitalisations; mortality came from ONS death registrations and hospitalisation outcomes from HES-APC.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, first hospitalisation, and the overall number of hospitalisations. ONS Death Registration Data was used to ascertain all-cause mortality, while the HES-APC dataset was used to capture hospitalisation related information.

concept.text: Primary outcomes: all-cause mortality, first hospitalisation, overall number of hospitalisations

canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes comprised 59 long-term conditions across 17 systems; for each outcome-specific sub-study, participants with that condition at baseline were excluded before weighting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary outcomes included 59 long-term conditions across 17 systems. For each sub-study created for each specific outcome, individuals with a record of the corresponding outcome condition at baseline were excluded before PSFS weighting.

concept.text: Incident 59 long-term health conditions across 17 systems

canonical_statement: The number of hospitalisations was analysed with negative binomial regression; all-cause mortality with Cox proportional hazards; other non-fatal outcomes with competing-risk Cox models using death as the competing event; estimates were combined across imputed datasets with Rubin rules.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For all other non-fatal outcomes, competing risk Cox proportional hazard regression models were used instead, with death as the competing event.

canonical_statement: Benjamini-Yekutieli correction was applied to p-values across multiple testing with a corrected significance level of 0.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To reduce the risk of type 1 error, the Benjamini-Yekutieli method for multiple testing was applied to correct p-values, in which a significance level of 0.05 was considered.
